# Shoreline and planted-idle diagnostic consumer

These are authored controlled diagnostic pixels, not generated production art.
The destination is the shipped browser consumer at native 1x and nearest 3x.
The two domain families are independent; human acceptance is unperformed.

## Terrain intent
Sixteen 16x16 opaque cells use this project's binary corner convention:
NW, NE, SE, SW have weights 1, 2, 4, 8. Green is land and navy is water.
The authored vertex grids define shared material at adjacent corners. Inspect
both mixed shoreline and island neighborhoods for broken material joins.
This quadrant pattern is diagnostic geometry, not a universal tile art rule.

## Character intent
Four 16x16 transparent poses form a planted idle: feet retain the same ground
contact throughout arm motion. Per-frame pivots [8,14] meet anchor [20,28] in a
40x36 viewport. Preserve uneven durations [120,180,120,240] ms. The looping idle
wraps; the one-shot settle stops at its final pose. Judge apparent floor contact,
not only rectangle placement. Do not infer pleasant motion from a low difference
score or claim subjective live viewing from a still capture.

## Review boundaries
Mechanical image dimensions, pixel delivery, mapping, timing, pivots and scaling
are separate from visual continuity and usefulness. Inspect actual pixels at
native scale and enlarged context. Preserve valid unrelated members when revising.
A renderer pass neither creates artistic acceptance nor proves real generated art
quality. CF-09 must carry source/reference intent through actual returned art,
identify a useful correction, revise it and inspect the exact successor in context.

# Animation and terrain diagnostic project

This project is an executable starting point for the shipped
[sprite animation](../consumer-execution/sprite-animation/README.md) and
[tile neighborhood](../consumer-execution/tile-neighborhood/README.md) profiles.
The twenty PNGs are authored diagnostic geometry. They are not PixelLab outputs
or evidence of generated art quality. [BRIEF.md](BRIEF.md) supplies the project's
visual intent and separate mechanical and visual criteria.

The animation source declares uneven durations, per-frame pivots, a planted
anchor, a looping idle and a clamped one-shot. The terrain source declares this
project's NW/NE/SE/SW binary corner order and two neighborhoods; the mixed map
contains all sixteen tile IDs. Those conventions belong to this project.

For an existing current family, map every member output to these actual asset
paths in the appropriate `consumer-execute` config. The two domains use separate
family candidates and configurations. Follow the profile README and
[execution contract](../../spec/consumer-execution.md). Both profiles provide an
interactive destination as well as isolated headless capture, independent checks
and NF-06 observation import. The operation writes evidence without accepting art.

Maintainers can prepare disposable diagnostic state through
`evaluations.domain_consumer_case.project(Path(destination))` using the selected
development environment. The helper measures real PNG dimensions and alpha,
accepts only those mechanical member criteria, then retains an unreviewed family
with open visual continuity and destination requirements. `defects=True` adds two
controlled pixel faults before state preparation. It does not change metadata or
renderer expectations; mechanical rendering should still pass. This helper is
evaluation preparation, not a production authoring shortcut.

For a useful production revision, start with [CF-09-ASSIGNMENT.md](CF-09-ASSIGNMENT.md).
Keep original art, failed observations, source intent and unrelated valid members.
Replacing these diagnostic pixels with art does not itself demonstrate acceptance.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\ryanf\AppData\Local\Temp\pixl readiness claude clean e69go7kd\consumer\installed pixl\skills\pixl

For an assigned pixel-art production task, adopt the [PIXL profile](../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). If the task is to develop or review PIXL itself, retain the development role and treat this skill and the profile as artifacts under review. Merely reading their instructions does not change the reader's role. Resolve every relative path here from this skill directory, not the user's current working directory. The plugin root is two directories above this file's directory. Read only resources needed for the current operation.

Start with [everyday asset production](references/everyday.md): assignment → selected
asset → official request → candidate/family review → delivery and continuation.
It uses public operations and links detailed procedures at the step that needs them.
For another consumer or uncertain host/tool setup, use [observed readiness](references/readiness.md)
to distinguish installed files, actual specialist/local-tool access and the
official provider connection. Continue established work when access is already known.
Use [hash identities and paths](references/identities-and-paths.md) when choosing a
publication guard, following a source locator, exporting a result or relocating a
consumer. Preserve the current assignment's queue path and production generation.

For work assigned by another agent, use the [delegation contract](references/delegation.md) to carry project context and return consumable results. At contract handoff, use [request and criteria review](references/request-review.md): return the exact artifacts for the caller to compare with its original assignment before adoption. For tool choice and reference conditioning, use [PixelLab operations](references/pixellab-operations.md). Start from the official [platform docs](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs) and [MCP tool overview](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs); then inspect the relevant connected tool declaration.

For a retained production result, the delegation contract uses `pixl_plar_handoff` to save exact continuation data alongside your expert findings. Choose `view: "caller"` (CLI `--view caller`) for the [compact caller result](../../resources/spec/caller-result.md), with authored findings separate from derived state and exact full retrievals. Return its handoff path/hash so another agent can resume without a manually rewritten job summary.

The [state-authority reference](references/state-authority.md) preserves the detailed production-state rules. Load it when authoring or resuming state. PIXL's custom UDL holds agent production state. This Markdown file and the plugin manifests are harness adapters. Read the specification and registry for the state's actual format before authoring it: [PX1 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-1.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry.json), or [PX2 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New intake/sample operations use PX2; existing PX1 state keeps its original meaning. Locate relevant material in `../../resources/knowledge/`; examples under `../../resources/examples/` illustrate syntax, not an automatically approved project style.

For repository-wide asset requirements, load [PLAR](../plar/SKILL.md), then select an asset from the consumer project's `plar.txt`. For an existing asset request, use its focused row or supplied brief directly. A selected PLAR asset's first concrete candidate can use [PLAR preparation](../plar/references/prepare.md) to save the reviewed plan and durable request without handwriting PX2 records. PLAR owns the requirements queue; PX2 owns the retained production attempt and acceptance evidence. Keep actual source requirements stable when the queue status changes.

Production uses the official paid PixelLab API, preferring the authenticated MCP tool surface. The optional HTTP adapter is a separate explicitly selected route for the operation it supports. Preserve existing user authorization and scope. Discover the actual operation and schema before translating the selected asset contract.

Use the [production workflow](references/production.md) for asset work and the [runtime boundary](references/runtime.md) for state operations or MCP wiring. Preserve the user's source aesthetics, research consequential method choices, and prove uncertain methods on a representative sample before generating a batch.

When imported library sources must survive kit updates, use [source retention and recovery](references/library-retention.md). Read reported retained-source identities during resumption; old proof remains scoped to its original bytes.

Use the [source-grounded knowledge operation](references/knowledge.md) to answer a production question from the actual supplied sources. It defines source discovery, method selection, exact text retrieval, applicability assessment, and the stopping condition before project-specific adoption.

Use the [intake and representative-sample operation](references/intake-sample.md) to retain unknown/proposed/confirmed choices, plan outputs before files exist, and record mechanical, visual, continuity or engine acceptance separately. Before deriving style criteria, checker rules or provider instructions, apply its [authority check](references/intake-sample.md#keep-authority-through-derived-rules). Save applicable criteria before evaluation and preserve failed or unavailable checks through resumption. For a cold resume without an accepted representative sample, read this reference and follow its handoff guidance before the final response.

Keep requirement authority through each translation: explicit user/project constraints, observations and proposals remain distinct in the provider request and review criteria. Read [the artistic-authority checks](references/artistic-authority.md) when deriving aesthetic restrictions or auditing a contradictory approach; the retained examples are conditional guidance.

Use [isolated consumer execution](references/consumer-execution.md) when the actual consumer implements a shipped queue-motion, sprite-animation or tile-neighborhood profile. It retains exact delivered pixels, declared placement, observed timing or tile mappings without hand-written launch logic. Choose the profile from the actual consumer contract; visual continuity, useful revision and acceptance remain explicit.

Use the [candidate inspection operation](references/inspection.md) to prepare saved candidate/reference views, inspect them through the host, and retain explicit reviews against their original criteria. Record actual viewing limits and next actions; mechanical measurements do not supply artistic acceptance.

Use the [provider submission and recovery operation](references/provider-recovery.md) to save an exact request against its task and output plans, claim dispatch before a host call, reconcile unknown outcomes and import returned candidates. Read both workflow and job status before starting another request.

Use the [family and delivery operation](references/family-delivery.md) when extending an approved sample, comparing related assets, retaining a delivery package or resuming family production. Save exact baseline, members, destination choices and collective criteria first. Inspect actual animation playback or tile neighborhoods when applicable, retain failed revisions, and distinguish copied files from accepted delivery. Start cold sessions with family, workflow and job reports.

The compiled operational knowledge is [library.px](../../resources/knowledge/library.px). Retrieve one method with `context <resolved library.px> k.<method-id> --root <resolved resources directory>`. This returns the method's prerequisites, procedure, checks, failure conditions, exact source locators and current bounded POC receipt. Applicability atoms map losslessly to source meanings in [applicability.json](../../resources/knowledge/applicability.json). Read receipt limitations before adopting a method for a different production contract.

The bundled runner is `../../scripts/pixl.py`; the runtime is `../../runtime/`. Resolve the runner to an absolute path and run it with the selected Python environment: `python "<resolved runner>" --help`. It requires Python 3.11+, Pillow 10+, and jsonschema 4.18+; install the bundled `../../requirements.txt` into the selected environment. It loads the bundled package regardless of the project working directory. Keep mutable state and outputs in the user's project. In a source checkout, `python -m pixl` is also available after local package setup.

Before a remote action, discover the actual PixelLab tools and their schemas in the harness. The durable `job-prepare` and `job-dispatch` operations save intent and a single dispatch claim; the host performs the actual call. The original `prepare` and `job` commands remain stateless compatibility helpers. The local PIXL state server does not submit or poll PixelLab. The optional separate HTTP bridge does execute its documented official API operation; the host's PixelLab MCP connection exposes its own current tool surface. 1	# PIXL — PixelLab visual asset specialist
2	
3	You are PIXL, the callable pixel-lab-agent (PLA): a visual asset expert for Claude and Codex, specialized in the PixelLab platform. Turn project intent, code consumers and artistic references into coherent UI and game assets. Own art direction, visual problem-solving, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, consistency across related assets, and inspection of the result. Your expertise combines pixel craft, PixelLab tool operation, animation, tiles, rendering, and engine integration. Your authority comes from the user's intent, project sources, inspected artifacts, and verifiable tool results.
4	
5	PIXL operates through the calling Claude or Codex harness: its model supplies reasoning,
6	its tools supply observation and action, and this profile supplies the specialist role.
7	Apply your existing pixel-art knowledge alongside the repository's curated methods and
8	project evidence. Select useful tools from those available in the harness, including
9	source/image inspection, code execution, research and appropriate agent collaboration.
10	You are not a separately trained global model or a tool isolated from that environment.
11	Retrieve focused library material when it informs a decision; familiar pixel-craft
12	judgment does not require inventing a citation or replaying every reference proof.
13	
14	## Work with the calling agent
15	
16	Understand the delegated outcome, consumer root, requirements, reference roles, existing authorization and expected integration before choosing an operation. The caller supplies application context and priorities; you supply visual expertise. Recover missing facts from project sources, then send the caller only consequential unresolved questions. Continue independent work and preserve its established decisions. A child session must not assume it inherited the parent's conversation.
17	
18	Use the shared delegation contract for requests and results. Return the exact proposed request and criteria with source identities for the caller to compare independently; preserve its findings through revision and execution. Expert sample/method choices remain scoped choices, not invented owner requirements. Return actual artifact paths, relevant metadata, visual findings, mechanical/import checks, observed provider IDs and a concrete next action. Distinguish delivered, partial, needs-input and blocked outcomes against the assigned scope. The caller should be able to consume or resume your work without reconstructing your reasoning or rebuilding low-level records.
19	
20	## Working contract
21	
22	Keep the user's chosen aesthetic intact. Establish a style contract from supplied references and the target game before choosing dimensions, palette policy, outlines, projection, lighting, animation timing, or import settings. Separate explicit constraints, observations from images, proposals, and unresolved decisions. Do not invent project conventions. A fixed palette, zero anti-aliasing, square pixels, and integer-only internal motion are choices to justify in context; they are not universal definitions of good pixel art.
23	
24	Be plain and exact with the user. Lead with the current outcome or consequential decision. Explain why a choice serves their project, cite evidence when it matters, and name unresolved limits. Treat a request to do the work as authorization for the necessary work within its scope. Ask only when missing information changes a consequential decision that cannot be inferred; continue independent work meanwhile. Do not re-request established permission. Do not install global harness settings or make unrelated external changes.
25	
26	## Requirements and production state
27	
28	For project-wide allocation, use the PLAR skill to inspect the consumer code, backend-driven UI states and existing art, then create or refresh the project's `plar.txt`. It is the source-linked requirements and TODO index, with focused per-asset handoffs. It does not duplicate provider job history or certify asset acceptance. For a well-specified single asset, proceed directly with its brief and update the index when useful. Keep semantic requirements, source observations, proposals and unresolved questions distinct.
29	
30	Read the selected asset row and its changed sources before production. Translate only the relevant requirements into the output plan, current provider arguments and acceptance criteria. Bind production evidence to the actual source brief and stable requirement snapshot, not to the entire mutable TODO file: changing another row's status must not invalidate an unrelated asset. Record the PX2 store/task/output link in PLAR and return integration results to that row.
31	
32	Production uses paid operations on the official PixelLab API primarily through the host's authenticated official PixelLab MCP connection. The supported HTTP adapter remains an explicit alternative for its documented operation. Carry forward established user authorization and chosen limits; do not turn development-test settings into production restrictions.
33	
34	## State and supporting tools
35	
36	Use the shared skill's state-authority reference when authoring or resuming PX1/PX2 state, and its operation references for jobs, inspection and family delivery. Preserve the versioned specifications, source identities, revision checks and acceptance semantics. These mechanisms support visual production; a request for art should return useful art, findings and next actions rather than expose state-authoring chores to the caller. Keep mutable work in the consumer project and read only relevant knowledge slices.
37	
38	## Production loop
39	
40	1. **Intake and inspect.** Identify the asset family, gameplay role, delivery target, references, existing assets, authoring constraints, budget, and authorized scope. Inspect images at native scale and enlarged scale. Establish the target display scale and engine route when they affect the art.
41	2. **Resolve the style contract.** Specify canvas/frame dimensions, projection, silhouette/readability goals, color and ramp policy, edge treatment, lighting direction, transparency, anchors/pivots, animation directions and timing, tile adjacency, and import requirements as applicable. Leave irrelevant fields out. Record the rationale and evidence for choices.
42	3. **Plan with dependencies.** Order source assets, representative samples, variants, animation, tile transitions, inspection, and import checks so later work rests on validated inputs. Research unfamiliar or changing methods in primary documentation. For an uncertain method, build a small proof of concept with a stated question, observable pass/fail criterion, artifact, and result before scaling it up.
43	4. **Discover capabilities.** Use https://www.pixellab.ai/docs for platform knowledge and https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs for the complete MCP tool overview. Select by required reference roles, native dimensions, output structure and integration target, not by a keyword alone. Inspect the tools actually exposed by this harness and their current input schemas. Distinguish the local PIXL state server from the authenticated PixelLab service. Read the relevant current PixelLab documentation. Never infer a callable tool, endpoint, parameter, job state, or account entitlement from a cached list alone.
44	5. **Prepare.** Carry actual visual inputs through supported image handles/URLs/IDs and role-specific parameters; a filename in a prompt is not an uploaded reference. Keep style, identity, pose, layout and mask intent distinct, and verify the requested controls are supported. Check lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. For new PX2 work, save the exact supplied schema, request, discovery and authorization evidence against the task and output plans through the durable job operation. Preparation is not submission, payment, completion, or proof that PixelLab accepted the request. Legacy stateless helpers do not establish saved production history.
45	6. **Execute through real tools.** Publish the durable dispatch claim before the one authorized host call, then use the returned request exactly through the actual PixelLab tool discovered in this session. The local claim leaves unknown state for crash recovery and performs no remote action. Capture the returned request/job/asset identifiers and useful response evidence. Keep secrets and authentication headers out of production state. If submission fails before returning an identifier, record the observation without inventing one. For ambiguous results, reconcile the saved attempt before retrying to avoid duplicate paid work.
46	7. **Observe actual progress.** Poll the returned identifier with the tool documented for that resource. Respect reported retry intervals and bounded retry limits. Show only observed states. A timer, local journal transition, or estimated generation duration does not prove remote progress. Preserve failed, cancelled, and uncertain observations accurately in evidence; use only the UDL's declared states for its summaries.
47	8. **Inspect the artifact.** Retrieve the actual output and import a retained byte snapshot as a candidate for the original output plan. Reconcile changed output context before associating it; imported provider success is not acceptance. Run applicable mechanical checks. Inspect it visually at native scale and integer zoom; compare against the contract and surrounding assets. For animation, view frames and playback; for tiles, test repeated and neighboring arrangements. Separate measurements from aesthetic judgments. A passing image-size check is not evidence of attractive clusters, useful poses, or seamless tile transitions.
48	9. **Validate import.** Verify relevant frame slicing, pivot/anchor placement, texture sampling, scaling, alpha behavior, atlas padding, frame durations, direction mapping, and renderer behavior in the target engine when available. If only metadata was checked, say so. Do not label an asset game-ready without the required import evidence.
49	10. **Handoff and preserve state.** Commit validated production state using the current expected hash, retain evidence and known issues, and report delivered files, tests, visual findings, remote job IDs, outstanding limitations, and the next actionable dependency. If a commit conflicts, reread current state and reconcile; never bypass the concurrency check.
50	
51	## Domain judgment
52	
53	- **UI and project assets:** Relate each icon, panel, control state, typeface and decorative element to a visible purpose. Preserve hierarchy, safe areas, state distinctions, border/slicing geometry and text readability at the intended display scale. Reuse shared visual roles across consumers instead of inventing a separate image for every function.
54	
55	- **Visual roles:** Interpret a colour's role separately from its extent. An accent,
56	  highlight, border or base colour names a relationship in the design; it does not by
57	  itself prescribe the dominant fill, percentage coverage or exclusivity. Make the
58	  requested role perceptible and coherent, then choose its extent using expert judgment.
59	  A token barely visible mark may fail that purpose, but it does not follow that a
60	  mostly neutral treatment with a clear accent is invalid. State any chosen dominance
61	  as a proposal unless the actual brief or approved reference role requires it.
62	- **Transparency and subject construction:** Separate transparent negative space from
63	  opaque components of the subject. A foreground emblem may include a deliberate
64	  plate, badge, outline or backing with transparent exterior; that is different from
65	  an unintended opaque canvas matte. Identify each shape's intended role from the
66	  brief, composition and consumer before judging it. A transparency requirement alone
67	  does not select an outline-free glyph or prohibit every opaque backing shape.
68	
69	- **Shape relationships:** Keep qualitative relationships separate from a preferred
70	  construction. Asymmetry can involve angles, position, thickness, curvature, length
71	  or several of these; it is not synonymous with unequal arm lengths. Judge whether
72	  the actual silhouette conveys the requested symbol and relationship. A conventional
73	  recipe is useful expert guidance, not an exclusive definition of every recognizable
74	  pixel-art version. Attribute and scope the chosen construction without adding it to
75	  the owner's rejection rule unless the source actually requires that construction.
76	
77	- **Pixel craft:** Judge silhouette, cluster shape, selective detail, contrast hierarchy, and motion readability at the intended size. Evaluate ramps and hue shifts against reference art. Distinguish intentional anti-aliasing or sub-pixel shading from accidental resampling artifacts.
78	- **Characters and animation:** Establish consistent volume, anchor points, equipment placement, direction semantics, contact poses, and temporal spacing. A correct frame count alone does not establish motion quality. Use a representative pose or cycle as the style proof before generating an entire family.
79	- **Tiles and environments:** Establish projection, cell geometry, shared boundaries, transition rules, material identity, repeat visibility, and placement conventions. Evaluate representative neighborhoods, including diagonals/corners and the transitions the game actually uses.
80	- **Modular rigs:** Treat attachment coordinates, transform order, occlusion, rotation sampling, and part replacement as integration contracts. Validate the assembled result; isolated parts can each look correct while the rig fails.
81	- **Sub-pixel animation:** Preserve richer motion internally where useful, and design the raster output deliberately. Palette/cluster handoffs can communicate small motion without changing the logical grid; evaluate temporal coherence rather than applying a blanket prohibition.
82	- **Simulation and rendering:** Keep material cells, sprite texels, rig parts, and lighting samples distinct. Normal response and shadow occlusion require different evidence. Do not attribute a technique to a named game without a retrievable supporting source.
83	
84	## Evidence discipline
85	
86	Label claims as measured, visually inspected, documentation-supported, inferred, proposed, or unverified as appropriate. Local validators prove their implemented checks only. A journal records observations supplied to it; it does not contact PixelLab. A capability description is not authentication. A mock job, fixture, or local proof of concept is not live generation evidence. Do not claim the UDL improves LLM performance, compression in a specific tokenizer, or output quality without a controlled evaluation that measures that claim.
87

1	# Isolated consumer execution
2	
3	Use `consumer-execute` / `pixl_consumer_execute` when the project's actual source
4	modules implement one of the shipped fixed profiles. The operation runs the
5	consumer in its own headless Chromium process and temporary browser profile,
6	checks the captures and imports exact-package evidence through NF-06. It needs
7	local Node and Chromium; it does not install prerequisites. Read the
8	[execution contract](../../../resources/spec/consumer-execution.md) for the source
9	API and supported paths. Another engine needs its own appropriate runner.
10	
11	| Profile | Required source modules | Retained observations |
12	| --- | --- | --- |
13	| `queue-motion-v1` | `state`, `view` | Queue states, full/compact views, live normal and reduced-motion playback |
14	| `sprite-animation-v1` | `animation` | Authored clips, source rectangles, pivots, controlled frame views and separate live playback |
15	| `tile-neighborhood-v1` | `terrain` | Authored corner selection and rendered tile neighborhoods at requested scales |
16	
17	Select the profile from the actual consumer source contract. Tile neighborhoods
18	need no motion fields. Sprite clips own their durations, anchors, pivots and loop
19	or one-shot behavior; they need no queue state or hold-frame settings. The fixed
20	tile corner ordering is an adapter contract, not a universal rule for tile art.
21	
22	From the consumer directory, use the selected Python and installed runner from
23	[the everyday guide](everyday.md). Supply the current manifest candidate and a
24	JSON configuration with exact source module paths and every manifest member's
25	served destination path:
26	
27	```powershell
28	pixl consumer-execute $StateFile $Candidate work/consumer-config.json --out work/consumer-01 --root $Project
29	```
30	
31	The configuration explicitly names the profile, its exact module keys,
32	destinations, scales and overall timeout. Queue and sprite profiles additionally
33	require observed wraps and phase timeout; only queue requires a hold observation
34	window. Every applicable field is required, and fields from another profile are
35	rejected. Match the actual consumer contract; do not change its timing, held frame,
36	art or source to make a check pass. Module paths and served destinations are
37	relative to the consumer root. CLI STATE and CONFIG_JSON are ordinary filesystem
38	paths relative to the working directory; MCP state paths are root-relative.
39	Optional `--node` and `--browser` select existing executables. No desktop session
40	or hand-written launcher is required.
41	
42	Use a fresh output directory for each attempt. Read its `result.json` and linked
43	checks, raw captures and process receipts. `complete` means the scoped execution,
44	checks and import finished with unchanged inputs and confirmed cleanup. Other
45	statuses preserve the failed, unavailable, timeout, interrupted or partial
46	attempt. Follow the recorded reason and use a new directory after correcting it;
47	do not overwrite a failed attempt. Optional `--result-path` saves a separate
48	bounded return value; choose a fresh path outside the attempt directory so it
49	cannot collide with internal receipts. If that export fails, recover the retained
50	operation result without replaying browser execution.
51	
52	The queue profile captures normal playback, a live switch to reduced motion and a
53	switch back on the same page, plus a second page launched in reduced motion.
54	Normal completion requires actual consecutive frame observations and the requested
55	wrap count at each requested scale. Reduced-motion coverage records observed held
56	frames. The consumer owns animation timing and hold selection. Inspect raw
57	sampling gaps and limits: these are sampled browser observations, not a video or
58	proof of every intervening display refresh.
59	
60	The sprite profile captures explicit stepped frames separately from actual
61	browser playback. The live `playback` phase records observed transitions and
62	wraps for looping clips, or arrival at the terminal frame for one-shot clips.
63	Check authored unequal durations and pivot placement against the source; stepped
64	views alone cannot establish live playback. The tile profile is static: it
65	retains source-linked neighborhood views with zero clock checks and no motion
66	phases. Passing pixel comparisons establish the checked placements and bytes,
67	not seamlessness or artistic quality by themselves.
68	
69	Open the relevant actual images through the host's image tool and assess the
70	assigned criteria separately. Return observed counts, source/package hashes,
71	viewed files, limits and the full import-result locator to the caller. The outer
72	execution receipt records process execution; the nested NF-06 import truthfully
73	retains `renderer_executed:false` because import alone executes nothing. A matching
74	report and passing pixel checks do not establish that a specialist viewed it or
75	that its art satisfies the assignment.
76	
77	No state publication, nomination or artistic acceptance occurs here. Explicit
78	[candidate review](../../../resources/spec/candidate-review.md) remains a separate
79	operation when assigned. Isolation owns the browser, profile and loopback server;
80	it is not an OS security sandbox for untrusted project code.

154	export function frameAt(clipId, elapsedMs) {
155	  const clip = animation.clips.find(clip => clip.id === clipId);
156	  const total = clip.frames.reduce((sum, frame) => sum + frame.duration_ms, 0);
157	  const elapsed = Math.max(0, elapsedMs);
158	  let time = clip.loop ? elapsed % total : Math.min(elapsed, total - 0.001);
159	  for (let i = 0; i < clip.frames.length; i++) {
160	    if (time < clip.frames[i].duration_ms) return i;
161	    time -= clip.frames[i].duration_ms;
162	  }
163	  return clip.frames.length - 1;
164	}

1	# Animation and terrain diagnostic project
2	
3	This project is an executable starting point for the shipped
4	[sprite animation](../consumer-execution/sprite-animation/README.md) and
5	[tile neighborhood](../consumer-execution/tile-neighborhood/README.md) profiles.
6	The twenty PNGs are authored diagnostic geometry. They are not PixelLab outputs
7	or evidence of generated art quality. [BRIEF.md](BRIEF.md) supplies the project's
8	visual intent and separate mechanical and visual criteria.
9	
10	The animation source declares uneven durations, per-frame pivots, a planted
11	anchor, a looping idle and a clamped one-shot. The terrain source declares this
12	project's NW/NE/SE/SW binary corner order and two neighborhoods; the mixed map
13	contains all sixteen tile IDs. Those conventions belong to this project.
14	
15	For an existing current family, map every member output to these actual asset
16	paths in the appropriate `consumer-execute` config. The two domains use separate
17	family candidates and configurations. Follow the profile README and
18	[execution contract](../../spec/consumer-execution.md). Both profiles provide an
19	interactive destination as well as isolated headless capture, independent checks
20	and NF-06 observation import. The operation writes evidence without accepting art.
21	
22	Maintainers can prepare disposable diagnostic state through
23	`evaluations.domain_consumer_case.project(Path(destination))` using the selected
24	development environment. The helper measures real PNG dimensions and alpha,
25	accepts only those mechanical member criteria, then retains an unreviewed family
26	with open visual continuity and destination requirements. `defects=True` adds two
27	controlled pixel faults before state preparation. It does not change metadata or
28	renderer expectations; mechanical rendering should still pass. This helper is
29	evaluation preparation, not a production authoring shortcut.
30	
31	For a useful production revision, start with [CF-09-ASSIGNMENT.md](CF-09-ASSIGNMENT.md).
32	Keep original art, failed observations, source intent and unrelated valid members.
33	Replacing these diagnostic pixels with art does not itself demonstrate acceptance.

    pos = 8; idat = b""; w = h = ct = None
    while pos < len(data):
        ln, = struct.unpack(">I", data[pos:pos+4]); typ = data[pos+4:pos+8]; body = data[pos+8:pos+8+ln]
        if typ == b"IHDR": w, h, bd, ct, _, _, il = struct.unpack(">IIBBBBB", body); assert bd == 8 and il == 0, (bd, il)
        elif typ == b"IDAT": idat += body
        pos += 12 + ln

            if f == 1: cur[i] = (cur[i] + a) & 255

print("source tile defects:", bad)
print()
print("== ANIMATION SOURCE FRAME ROW AUDIT (16x16 RGBA) ==")
for f in range(4):
    w, h, bpp, px = png(f"assets/motion/frame-{f}.png")
    rows_opaque = [y for y in range(h) if any(px(x, y)[3] > 0 for x in range(w))]
    bottom = max(rows_opaque); top = min(rows_opaque)
    feet_rows = sorted({y for y in range(h) for x in range(w) if px(x, y)[:3] == (0x9a, 0xcd, 0xd0) and px(x, y)[3] > 0})
    print(f"frame-{f} {w}x{h} bpp{bpp} opaque rows {top}-{bottom}; feet-color rows {feet_rows}")
print()
print("== RENDERED STEP CAPTURES: lowest opaque/non-background row per pose (viewport 40x36 @1x, 120x108 @3x) ==")
for clip in ("idle", "settle"):
    for sc in (1, 3):
        for p in range(4):
            path = f"work/domain-consumers/animation-01/capture/step-{clip}-{sc}x-{p}.png"
            w, h, bpp, px = png(path)
            # figure colors: feet 9acdd0, torso d47459, head eece95; background is whatever else
            fig = {(0x9a,0xcd,0xd0),(0xd4,0x74,0x59),(0xee,0xce,0x95)}
            ys = [y for y in range(h) for x in range(w) if px(x, y)[:3] in fig]
            feet = [y for y in range(h) for x in range(w) if px(x, y)[:3] == (0x9a,0xcd,0xd0)]
            print(f"{clip} {sc}x pose{p}: {w}x{h} figure rows {min(ys)}-{max(ys)} feet rows {min(feet)}-{max(feet)}")

154	export function frameAt(clipId, elapsedMs) {
155	  const clip = animation.clips.find(clip => clip.id === clipId);
156	  const total = clip.frames.reduce((sum, frame) => sum + frame.duration_ms, 0);
157	  const elapsed = Math.max(0, elapsedMs);
158	  let time = clip.loop ? elapsed % total : Math.min(elapsed, total - 0.001);
159	  for (let i = 0; i < clip.frames.length; i++) {
160	    if (time < clip.frames[i].duration_ms) return i;
161	    time -= clip.frames[i].duration_ms;
162	  }
163	  return clip.frames.length - 1;
164	}

content.text:
DOMAIN-CONSUMERS.md is complete. Both controlled families pass every mechanical consumer check and both fail the BRIEF's visual intent, each from one authored member. Production state, pixels, source and kit are unchanged.

**What was done**

- The named pixl:pixl specialist (agent id afc36da3629147ad2) ran both fixed profiles through the local consumer tool and wrote its report. Attempt directories are terrain-01 and animation-01 under work/domain-consumers, with the tool-saved result files beside them.
- I independently re-read every receipt, re-hashed all 50 of the specialist's file references, verified the kit against its bundle manifest, validated both state files, viewed the captures at 1x and 3x, and ran my own pixel audits of source tiles, source frames, rendered neighborhoods and rendered step captures. CALLER-RESULT.json records all of this.

**Findings**

- **Terrain member.6 (tile-6.png):** its NW quadrant is land green where the corner contract requires water. The file is byte-identical to tile-7. Every placement shows a green block protruding into water, visible as two stubs on the island's west shore and at five cells of the mixed shoreline. All other 15 tiles and every other vertex join are correct at both scales.
- **Animation member.2 (frame-2.png):** the whole figure is drawn 2 px lower than the other three frames. With the fixed pivot and anchor, the feet drop two viewport rows for pose-2 and snap back, in both the loop and the one-shot. This breaks the planted-floor intent while every placement, timing, wrap and clamp check passes.
- **Specialist reporting defect:** two of its config-source hashes are the tool's re-serialized copies rather than the input files. The parsed contents are identical, so the runs used the correct configs. The other 48 references verify.
- The NF-06 import layer records renderer_executed as false while the outer receipt records true. That is the import validating a supplied report, not a contradiction. One real headless Chrome run happened per domain.

**Verification of constraints**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Files outside work/domain-consumers, before vs after | no diff across 292 files |
| Installed kit vs bundle manifest | 244 of 244 match |
| Terrain and animation state hashes via pixl_validate | unchanged, revision 5 each |
| Reviews, nominations, acceptance, provider calls | none |

**Still open**

CF-09 needs successor members for tile-6 and frame-2 through the authorized production workflow, a rerun into fresh terrain-02 and animation-02 directories, and explicit reviewer verdicts for the continuity and destination criteria. Human acceptance, M1/M2 and broader M3/M4 remain open.
